fullPassage:
Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your listener?
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
